title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
domain: math reasoning (reasoning-trace termination), fault repair, multimodal transfer
tasks_benchmarks: DeepScaleR practice/held-out split (490 x 8 answers, 200 x 1)

headline_result.text: In the best of eight sessions (session 8), Qwen3.5-27B's self-written edit (time-step bias +0.5 in all 48 linear-attention layers) raised held-out accuracy from 57.2% to 63.8% (+6.6 points) on 490 problems; three of eight sessions submitted an edit and two were significant; the first-protocol edit gave +1.1 points.
headline_result.quote: On the 490 held-out problems, the edit of session 8 solves 63.8% against 57.2%, with 439 answers right only with the edit against 182 only without it

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 8 sessions (second protocol, 27B); single session per size in first protocol; held-out 490 problems x 8 answers

key_claims.claim: Both significant self-edits target answers that run out of tokens; the larger gain comes from one uniform bias change to every linear-attention layer.
key_claims.quote: The larger gain comes from one uniform change: it raises the time-step bias of every linear-attention layer by 0.5, and with it fewer of its answers run out of tokens.

key_claims.claim: Under the first protocol, the 27B self-edit (removing 5% of a measured direction at layer 8) gave a small preregistered held-out gain, 57.2% to 58.3% (p = 0.038).
key_claims.quote: The self-edited model solves 58.3% of the answers and the base model 57.2%, p = 0.038 (Tab. 8).

key_claims.claim: Given a copy with eight noise-corrupted rows, the 27B model located the damaged matrix by a max/median statistic and clipped it, restoring held-out accuracy from 0.0% to 33.0% (base 58.5%).
key_claims.quote: On the 200 held-out problems, the damaged copy solves 0.0%, the repaired copy 33.0% and the base model 58.5%: the repair recovers about 56% of the base model’s accuracy

key_claims.claim: The text-found repair carried over to six image benchmarks (7.3% to 70.2%, base 84.3%).
key_claims.quote: On every benchmark the repaired copy solves far more than the damaged copy: 70.2% against 7.3% over the 600 problems, 83% of the base model’s 84.3%

key_claims.claim: Smaller models fail: 2B makes no edit, 4B and 9B break themselves (9B drops from 47.5% to 0.0% on held-out problems).
key_claims.quote: The 4B and 9B models edit themselves and break themselves

key_claims.claim: In five of eight second-protocol sessions the model withdrew, so the reported gains come from three submitted edits.
key_claims.quote: In five the model withdraws: three times it ends with no edit, after its own tests rejected every edit it tried (sessions 3, 4 and 7)

limitations_stated.text: Generation is not exactly reproducible; reruns with the same weights and seeds diverge.
limitations_stated.quote: Generation is not exactly reproducible: run twice with the same weights and the same seeds, two answers begin alike and then part ways

limitations_stated.text: Python sessions were not sandboxed from the file system in the first protocol; the authors audited code runs post hoc.
limitations_stated.quote: nothing blocks it from reading files, environment variables or the framework’s own modules.

limitations_stated.text: Three further sessions were stopped before their end and are not analysed.
limitations_stated.quote: Three further sessions of a model on its own weights were stopped before their end and are not analysed.

notes_for_review: First self-rewriting study: Qwen3.5 models edit their own weights via code with gradients blocked, with paired tests, a prespecified 490 x 8 held-out evaluation, and a deliberately damaged copy as a known-cause test. The gains target the same failure as MIT's Qwen edit (answers that run out of tokens/loop at the budget), and the biggest edit is a uniform bias shift; no random-direction control, no decoding baseline (e.g. presence penalty or thinking budget) and no fine-tuning comparison are reported, so whether an LLM is needed is untested. The headline +6.6 is the best of eight sessions (the first-protocol edit gave +1.1). The repair result mainly shows that an outlier-clipping rule fixes a planted 200-sigma corruption, which a simple norm check would also flag. Promotional framing ('Era of Self-Rewriting') exceeds the evidence.
